html:
SMTO-FIL-0006 — This computer can't list connected drives for SMTO

GUID: 3253fcbd-3920-42e8-a96d-753f05f8ddda
Slug: file-capability-unavailable
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO can only find USB and external drives by itself on Linux computers. The Gateway you're using runs a different system, so SMTO couldn't list its drives.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Gateway computer is a Mac, tell SMTO the exact folder on the drive to save to, starting with a slash, for example "copy the files to /Volumes/Backup" on a Mac. When you name the folder yourself, SMTO doesn't need to list the drives.
  2. If the drive can be plugged into a Linux computer that has a Gateway, choose that Gateway in the Execution target menu in the composer. SMTO can find drives by itself only on Linux computers.
  3. If neither works, for example on a Windows computer, ask the person who manages SMTO whether Removable destination protection in Settings › Security should stay on for this computer. That setting is what makes SMTO look for drives before saving, and only a manager should decide to change it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO saves to the folder you named, or asks you which drive to use.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and say which kind of computer the drive is plugged into.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Removable-destination inventory is implemented only for Linux Gateways; on this Gateway platform discovery reports capability_unavailable.

What this means

  • The removable-destination inventory implementation is called on a platform other than Linux and reports this discovery capability unavailable. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The removable-destination inventory implementation is called on a platform other than Linux and reports this discovery capability unavailable.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the Gateway platform and advertised discovery capability rather than assuming all file operations are unavailable.

How to fix it

  • Have the user name an explicit absolute POSIX destination path (bound directly without inventory; Windows drive-letter paths are not recognized as explicit destinations), target a Linux Gateway, or, as an administrative decision, turn off removable_destination_guard_enabled (Settings › Security › Removable destination protection) for this installation.
  • Use supported explicit destination selection or a Gateway advertising removable-destination discovery.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Use an advertised supported destination-selection flow on the intended platform.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
